title: TIDFormer: Exploiting Temporal and Interactive Dynamics Makes A Great Dynamic Graph Transformer

problem.claim: Dynamic graph neural networks need to capture sequential evolution and both temporal and interactive dynamics in dynamic graphs.

gap.claim: Existing Transformer-based dynamic graph neural networks vary substantially in effectiveness and efficiency, and their self-attention mechanisms have been defined opaquely on dynamic graphs.

contributions.claim: TIDFormer is a dynamic graph Transformer designed to exploit temporal and interactive dynamics efficiently.
The authors clarify and verify the interpretability of the proposed self-attention mechanism for dynamic graphs.

The model represents temporal dynamics with calendar-based time partitions, interaction dynamics with sampled first-order-neighbor embeddings for bipartite and non-bipartite graphs, and jointly models them through a simple decomposition.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report extensive experiments on several dynamic graph datasets.
The authors report that TIDFormer outperforms state-of-the-art models across most datasets and experimental settings.
The authors report significant efficiency advantages over previous Transformer-based methods.

narrative_sequence.summary: Transformer architectures are used in dynamic graph neural networks to capture sequential graph evolution.
Prior Transformer-based approaches differ in effectiveness and efficiency, motivating better self-attention definitions and comprehensive encoding of dynamic information.
TIDFormer combines an interpretable self-attention mechanism with calendar-based temporal partitioning, sampled-neighbor interaction embeddings, and decomposition-based joint modeling.
Experiments on several dynamic graph datasets are reported to show effectiveness and efficiency, including broad performance and efficiency gains.

source_observation.claim: The model represents temporal and interactive dynamics using calendar-based partitions, sampled first-order neighbors, and a simple decomposition.

interpretation.claim: Careful feature construction and simple joint modeling may capture multiple dynamic aspects without adding complex modules.

application.claim: For dynamic graph modeling, consider explicit temporal partitioning and interaction representations before introducing additional complex architectural components.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether these design choices transfer to other graph tasks, datasets, or settings.
